key_insight: Hierarchical multipoint anchoring strengthens buried interfaces in inverted perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and resistance to thermal cycling.
engineering_relevance: Engineering adhesion at transparent-conductor/SAM interfaces offers a route to reducing thermo-mechanical failure in high-efficiency perovskite photovoltaics.
method: Pretreat transparent conductive oxides with a homometallic halide to increase surface hydroxyl species.
Guide ordered self-assembled monolayer (SAM) assembly and multipoint metal–oxygen anchoring.
Use cooperative chloride-induced hydrogen bonding to reinforce interfacial robustness.
evidence_signal: Devices reached 27.3% efficiency (26.9% certified) and retained 94% of initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles from −40 to 85 °C under ISOS-T-3.
watch_item: Thermal-cycling results do not alone establish long-term outdoor or module-scale durability.
paper_title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
